19.0.s.en: 1. The flight of the Holy Family:

19.0.0.en: 1 The burden of Egypt. Behold, the LORD rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it.

19.0.1.en: We find no country that the Holy Bible speaks of as much as Egypt, after Canaan. The reason is that Israel, as a nation and a people, dwelt in Egypt, and the Jews lived there about 400 years, and finally went out with a high arm (*). By their going out through the blood of the lambs they became a symbol of the whole world, set free from the bondage of the devil through the blood of Christ, the unique slain Sacrifice. Egypt came to represent the power of the world in general, and the house of bondage from which He saves His people.

19.0.2.en: Isaiah opened his prophecy concerning Egypt in a way joyful for Egypt, saying: "Behold, the LORD rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it" [1].

19.0.3.en: St. Cyril the Great sees that the light, swift cloud (the Septuagint) is St. Mary, whom the Spirit of the Lord sanctified, so that she became light and uplifted, carrying the Lord of glory Jesus to flee with Him to Egypt from the face of Herod (Mt 2:13-15)... At His entering, the idols trembled and pagan worship was shaken, and the heart of the Egyptians melted with love, to receive Him dwelling among them; for he says: [The shining cloud that carried the Lord Jesus to Egypt is His mother the Virgin Mary, who surpassed the clouds in purity and holiness. And the altar that was set up to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt is the Christian Church, which arose upon the ruins of the pagan temples, after its idols were shaken and its temples collapsed before the face of the Lord Jesus]. For this reason the Church sings on the feast of the entry of the Lord Christ into Egypt: [Rejoice and be glad, O Egypt, with your children and all your borders, for He who loves mankind, who is before all ages, has come to you].

19.0.4.en: Although Egypt, with its Pharaoh and its pagan worship, represented the ancient pagan world in its violence and abominations, it was also a refuge for many, especially in times of famine. Our father Abraham came to it (Gen 12:10), and it received Joseph, persecuted by his brothers, to become the second man after Pharaoh, supplying from its storehouses all the surrounding lands; and to it came our father Jacob and his sons, where the nucleus of the people of God of old began, and the twelve tribes within it; and there appeared their first leader, Moses, great among the prophets, supported by the first high priest. Among the prophets who came to Egypt was the prophet Jeremiah, who urged the people not to flee to Egypt, but they forced him to accompany them on their journey to it (Jer 41:1; 43:7), and he uttered his last prophecies in Tahpanhes (Tahpanes) in Egypt (Jer 43:8-13). But when the heavenly Lord Christ came to our earth, He established His Church in it, to be colored with the spirit of divine blessing, so that its worship, its rites and its hymns came bearing the melody of heavenly life.

19.0.5.en: Egypt, which was filled with pagan worship, where it set up the Apis calf, cats, crocodiles and frogs... as gods, received the Lord of glory in it, and He raised up from the hearts of the Egyptians a sanctuary for Himself. Egypt was transformed, in a short period, from being the greatest stronghold of paganism into the greatest center of Christian thought, spiritual worship and evangelical life. The star of the Church of Egypt shone through the School of Alexandria, teacher of theology and of the interpretation of the Holy Bible to the early Christian world, and leader of the movement defending the right faith on an ecumenical level. And from Egypt the movement of Christian monasticism in all its forms set out, to draw the heart of the Church to the wilderness, to practice the inner, angelic life, at the very time when the doors of the imperial court were opened to the men of religion, and danger pursued the Church, where the spiritual, churchly work was mixed with temporal and political authority. The Church of Egypt carried the cross of her Bridegroom through the generations and offered countless numbers of martyrs and confessors; sometimes whole cities were martyred, and many vied with one another to obtain the crowns of martyrdom with joy and gladness of heart...

19.1.0.en: 2 And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom. 3 And the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof; and I will destroy the counsel thereof: and they shall seek to the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards. 4 And the Egyptians will I give over into the hand of a cruel lord; and a fierce king shall rule over them, saith the Lord, the LORD of hosts. 5 And the waters shall fail from the sea, and the river shall be wasted and dried up. 6 And the rivers shall stink, and the brooks of Egypt shall be weakened and dried up: the reeds and flags shall wither. 7 The paper reeds by the brooks, by the mouth of the brooks, and every thing sown by the brooks, shall wither, be driven away, and be no more. 8 The fishers also shall mourn, and all they that cast angle into the brooks shall lament, and they that spread nets upon the waters shall languish. 9 Moreover they that work in fine flax, and they that weave white cloth, shall be confounded. 10 And the pillars thereof shall be crushed, and all that work for hire shall be sick in soul. 11 Surely the princes of Zoan are fools, the counsel of the wise counsellors of Pharaoh is become brutish: how say ye unto Pharaoh, I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings? 12 Where are they? where are thy wise men? and let them tell thee now, and let them know what the LORD of hosts hath purposed upon Egypt. 13 The princes of Zoan are become fools, the princes of Noph are deceived; they have also seduced Egypt, even they that are the stay of the tribes thereof. 14 The LORD hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof: and they have caused Egypt to err in every work thereof, as a drunken man staggereth in his vomit. 15 Neither shall there be any work for Egypt, which the head or tail, branch or rush, may do. 16 In that day shall Egypt be like unto women: and it shall be afraid and fear because of the shaking of the hand of the LORD of hosts, which he shaketh over it. 17 And the land of Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt, every one that maketh mention thereof shall be afraid in himself, because of the counsel of the LORD of hosts, which he hath determined against it.

19.1.1.en: The flight of the Holy Family to Egypt and the setting up of an altar to the Lord there does not mean covering over its evils, but on the contrary, the Lord's revealing its weaknesses and spiritual wounds, so that He may remove from it every weakness (the kingdom of evil) and establish what is new (the Kingdom of God). The Lord's coming to it means the demolition of its idols and the removal of its abominations for the sake of the sanctification of its people.

19.1.2.en: He has brought out the fruits of the ancient abominations, namely:

19.1.3.en: First: the rise of civil wars, "And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom. And the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof" [2-3]. This is the natural fruit of its withdrawal from God, the Giver of inner peace, love and unity, for wars break out at the level of persons, even between friends, and at the level of cities and kingdoms [for there was a kingdom in Upper Egypt and another in Lower Egypt]. Evil shatters the inner soul and brings it into a state of despair and frustration.

19.1.4.en: Our withdrawal from God makes us lose our inner harmony, so that our inner life turns into a battlefield, and the body wrestles against the spirit, and the inner energies are not in harmony together... and the heart becomes an unbearable hell. On the contrary, when the Spirit of God takes the lead, man submits to Him wholly and lives in harmony and concord: the body supports the soul in its worship, and the senses and emotions are sanctified to work together with the pure mind, with a holy and good will in the Lord.

19.2.0.en: Second: the loss of true wisdom. The Egyptians were known as a very intelligent people, and the Holy Bible testifies that Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians (Acts 7:20), but their withdrawal from God made them lose everything, so that neither their wisdom nor their knowledge nor their civilization helped them, and they resorted to the idols to seek counsel: "I will destroy the counsel thereof: and they shall seek to the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards" [3].

19.3.0.en: Third: suffering under fierce rulers [4], who incline to domination and control rather than to serving the people and building the country. For when the hearts of the people grow hard through their distance from God, the Giver of kindness and goodness, He permits them violent leaders, so that as they do, so it is done to them.

19.3.1.en: When our inner heart grows hard toward others, we should expect nothing but that with the same measure with which we measure to others it will be measured to us; therefore He permits us to fall under violent leaders. This is what happens even in our daily life, in work, in the family and in our personal life... for he who is harsh to his parents will find his body violent in its fleshly warfare against the soul. What we sow for others we reap in our personal life.

19.4.0.en: Fourth: suffering from a state of drought, "And the waters shall fail from the sea, and the river shall be wasted and dried up. And the rivers shall stink, and the brooks of Egypt shall be weakened and dried up: the reeds and flags shall wither... The fishers also shall mourn, and all they that cast angle into the brooks shall lament... Moreover they that work in fine flax, and they that weave white cloth, shall be confounded. And the pillars thereof shall be crushed, and all that work for hire shall be sick in soul" [5-10].

19.4.1.en: It is as though evil bears the fruit of bitterness even in man's daily life and his essential needs, for the river Nile dries up [in many towns of Upper Egypt it is still called "the sea"], so that people find no water to drink, nor for farming, and the fishermen lose their work and lament in vain; and this affects industry and trade... So the great men, who are the pillars of Egypt, are crushed, and the souls of the slaves who work for the rich are depressed.

19.4.2.en: Through evil, ruin and corruption creep into the natural resources (the water) and the human energies of all classes! Man loses the water that waters his soul, and the fish that satisfies him inwardly, and the linen garments that cover his depths, and his inner peace; and thus he suffers thirst, hunger, nakedness and shame!

19.5.0.en: Fifth: the loss of the wise and the counsellors. Man does not suffer only from material deprivation, but from wise helpers who would support him in his distress. Therefore it is said: "Surely the princes of Zoan are fools, the counsel of the wise counsellors of Pharaoh is become brutish: how say ye unto Pharaoh, I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings? Where are they? where are thy wise men? and let them tell thee now, and let them know what the LORD of hosts hath purposed upon Egypt" [11-12].

19.6.0.en: In place of the wisdom for which Egypt was known, foolishness has come, even in Zoan, the capital of ancient northern Egypt. It was said: "And Solomon's wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt" (1 Kgs 4:30)... But this wisdom passes away when man withdraws from his God, the Source of wisdom; therefore the wise counsellors of Pharaoh give brutish counsel, that is, fleshly thoughts (1 Cor 2). And the sign of their deprivation of wisdom is the inability of the wise men to grasp the plan of God, the LORD of hosts, concerning Egypt [12]; how then can the people of God trust the counsel of Pharaoh concerning an alliance together against Assyria?!

19.7.0.en: "The princes of Noph are deceived; they have also seduced Egypt, even they that are the stay of the tribes thereof" [13]. This is the calamity of Egypt, that it accepted error as wisdom, for the princes of the capital of Upper Egypt (southern Egypt), Menouf (Memphis), were deceived by the noble wise men, who correspond to the hypocritical false prophets of whom the prophet Jeremiah often spoke.

19.8.0.en: Sixth: the loss of awareness and the entering into a state of drunkenness; "The LORD hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof: and they have caused Egypt to err in every work thereof, as a drunken man staggereth in his vomit" [14].

19.8.1.en: Since sin is intoxicating and makes man lose his awareness and his purpose in life, when he drinks its cup God permits a spirit of error to come upon him, so that he staggers like a drunkard, without purpose. He has no serious work for building himself and building others, whether great or despised, branch or rush (reed). And this is the most dangerous point to which man can come, for he thereby loses his human being and lives like one dead, with no taste for life.

19.9.0.en: Seventh: confusion in a state of fear, "In that day shall Egypt be like unto women: and it shall be afraid and fear because of the shaking of the hand of the LORD of hosts, which he shaketh over it" [16]. Pharaoh, who counts himself in arrogance and pride the rescuer of Israel and Judah from the hand of Assyria, is terrified, he and his men, and they become like women before the LORD of hosts and before Judah [17].

19.9.1.en: It is as though the Lord encourages Judah not to be terrified by the words of Pharaoh, and not to enter into an alliance with him as Israel and Aram did, for Pharaoh himself is terrified, not before Assyria, but before Judah itself.

19.10.s.en: 3. The setting up of an altar to the Lord:

19.10.0.en: 18 In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the LORD of hosts; one shall be called, The city of the sun. 19 In that day shall there be an altar to the LORD in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the LORD. 20 And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the LORD because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour and a defender, and he shall deliver them. 21 And the LORD shall be known to Egypt, and the Egyptians shall know the LORD in that day, and shall do sacrifice and oblation; yea, they shall vow a vow unto the LORD, and perform it. 22 And the LORD shall smite Egypt: he shall smite and heal it: and they shall return even to the LORD, and he shall be intreated of them, and shall heal them. 23 In that day shall there be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and the Assyrian shall come into Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria, and the Egyptians shall serve with the Assyrians. 24 In that day shall Israel be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, even a blessing in the midst of the land: 25 Whom the LORD of hosts shall bless, saying, Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.

19.10.1.en: After God revealed the wounds of Egypt and what sin had done to it, the loss of inner unity and of true wisdom, together with the suffering from the cruelty of the ruler and the cruelty of nature (drought), the confusion of its economy (agriculture and industry), the incapacity of its leading human energies, and even its entering into a state of unconsciousness and drunkenness, with fear and confusion even before Judah, the small kingdom, God intervenes to heal its wounds and save it, giving it the following blessings:

19.10.2.en: A. A new language: "In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the LORD of hosts; one shall be called, The city of the sun" [18]. These five cities are none other than the senses of the believer; for when the Gentiles come to faith in the Lord Christ, they hand over the five senses into His hands to be sanctified, to speak the language of the Spirit instead of the language of the flesh, and it is said to them as it was said to the Apostle Peter: "Thy speech bewrayeth thee" (Mt 26:73; Mk 14:70).

19.10.3.en: The heart of the believer is lifted up to the heavenly Canaan not only during his participation in the sacrament of the Eucharist and all the living liturgies of the Church, but also during his private worship, and even throughout his daily life, even in the moments of his eating, drinking and sleeping. This is the work of the Holy Spirit of God in our life; He carries us to heaven that we may experience it in our depths, and our language becomes Canaanite, that is heavenly, the language of love and inner joy. We share with the heavenly ones their liturgies and their constant joy, and we are not a people "of a strange speech" (Ezek 3:5).

19.10.4.en: B. Swearing by the name of the LORD of hosts; what does it mean: "swear to the LORD of hosts" [18]?

19.10.5.en: Swearing was a sign of trust and faith in the one by whose name man swears; so instead of swearing by pagan gods, the Gentiles, headed by Egypt, accept faith in the LORD of hosts, and the Egyptians hold fast to His name, counting this the secret of their strength.

19.10.6.en: C. The calling of one of the cities "the city of the sun" [8], meaning "Heliopolis," which was a center of sun worship; it turned from the worship of the material sun to the worship of the Sun of Righteousness who rises upon those who sit in darkness.

19.10.7.en: In the Septuagint it came as "the city of righteousness," for it bears the righteousness of Christ in us.

19.11.0.en: D. The setting up of an altar to the Lord: "In that day shall there be an altar to the LORD in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the LORD" [19]. By this is meant the altar of the Church of the New Testament, for the altar of the Old Testament was in Jerusalem and it was not permitted to offer sacrifices to the Lord outside it. The Holy Family crossed into Upper Egypt and hid for about six months in the place where the Monastery of the Virgin, famous as Al-Muharraq, now stands, which is considered to be in the middle of Egypt; in it a church was established to the Lord and the sacrifice of the Eucharist is offered upon it, which is a participation in the very sacrifice of the Cross.

19.12.0.en: As for the pillar at its border, it is St. Mark the Apostle, who came to Alexandria (on the border of Egypt) to preach the Gospel and to set up the altar of the Church of the New Testament, that the Egyptians might enjoy salvation from the enemy of good who oppressed them, and the Lord Himself would be their defender, intercessor and deliverer [20].

19.13.0.en: E. Spiritual knowledge: "And the LORD shall be known to Egypt, and the Egyptians shall know the LORD in that day" [21]. The Egyptians were concerned with spiritual knowledge, and the School of Alexandria was established for this purpose, to spread the knowledge of the Lord not through abstract rationalistic thoughts, but through a life of devotion and asceticism and the experience of communion with God the Father in His Son Jesus Christ by His Holy Spirit.

19.13.1.en: Knowledge was mingled with worship, as the prophet continues: "and shall do sacrifice and oblation; yea, they shall vow a vow unto the LORD, and perform it" [21].

19.13.2.en: Perhaps the most wonderful to write on the connection of knowledge with worship, as with evangelical conduct in daily life, is St. Clement of Alexandria, for this thought runs as a golden thread through all his writings. Among his words about knowledge (Gnosis):

19.13.3.en: [These are the marks that distinguish our Gnosis: first contemplation, then the fulfilling of the commandments, and finally the teaching of the righteous. When these traits are found in a man, he is counted a perfect gnostic. If a man loses one of these traits, his Gnosis is disabled].

19.14.0.en: F. Inner healing: "And the LORD shall smite Egypt: he shall smite and heal it: and they shall return even to the LORD, and he shall be intreated of them, and shall heal them" [22].

19.14.1.en: God permits its smiting, that is, its chastening for the weakness in it, that it may discover itself and realize its need of the Savior, and return to Him and find Him the Physician who alone is able to heal the wounds of the soul and restore its peace... Our Christ came as Physician and medicine at the same time:

19.14.2.en: * Blessed is the "Physician" who came down and cut without pain, healed our wounds with a medicine that is not bitter, for He showed His Son as a "medicine" that heals sinners!

19.14.3.en: St. Ephrem the Syrian. The Lord came to Egypt and struck its idols, that the Egyptians might find in Him the only secret of their healing.

19.14.4.en: G. Since the world conflict at that time was between Assyria and Egypt, and the other nations, among them Israel, were victims of this conflict, the coming of the Lord of glory Jesus gives peace to all, and all feel - in Christ Jesus - that the earth belongs to the Lord and to His Christ, and is not a center of dispute, and all share together in worship.

19.15.0.en: In a wonderful picture of this peace the prophet says: "In that day shall there be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and the Assyrian shall come into Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria, and the Egyptians shall serve with the Assyrians. In that day shall Israel be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, even a blessing in the midst of the land: whom the LORD of hosts shall bless, saying, Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance" [24].

19.15.1.en: What does "in that day," which is repeated about five times in verses [18-25], mean, if not the fullness of time in which the Lord Christ came to accomplish these blessings for us? He came as "the Way" in which the Gentiles gather to enjoy the spirit of spiritual unity and the abundance of blessing.

19.15.2.en: What does the gathering of Egypt, Assyria and Israel together in enjoying the divine blessing and the eternal inheritance mean? It is a symbolic picture of the universal Church, which brought enemies together in the spirit of love and unity. Israel was at that time in conflict between allying with Egypt or Assyria, the two opposing world powers of that time. But the coming of the Lord Christ solved the problem, for all became members of one Church enjoying the divine work, and the Egyptians were called the people of God, and Assyria the work of His hands, and Israel His inheritance.
